## Rules (Joa, 2 Sep 2026) **What you score.** Every candidate, same 12 topics, same measures inside them. You are measuring distance from the written Program, not picking a favourite. **What counts, in order.** 1. **Actions.** If they held office and a sourced vote or decision contradicts a 2026 promise, the action counts. 2. **Words.** A 2026 campaign sentence with a URL and a date. 3. **Silence.** No public answer is a dash. A dash is unknown, not a fail. **When a letter appears.** Only after 5 scored answers (across the 55 measures that sit in the 12). Under 5, they stay a dash. The number next to the letter is how many measures have a scored answer. **What the letter is.** One overall mark (Decision 14: B+, B, C, D, or —). It is not an endorsement and not a ranking of people. Area columns stay blank. The five doors on the front (tax cap, downtown order, housing, household bill, written program) are said / record / yes / dash — a sourced sentence or a fact, never a second grade. ### Filling a cell - **answer** = the mark (Aligned 3.0 · Close 2.0 · Partial+ 1.5 · Partial 1.0 · Weak 0.5 · Opposed −1.0) or `📋 Record` or `—`. - **quote or fact** = one verbatim sentence, or the vote / decision in one line. - **URL + date** = the source and its date (vote date, or page lastmod plus retrieved date). No URL + date = dash. - **Actions over words:** when a sourced vote or decision contradicts the 2026 sentence, score the action and put the sentence under it as context. A sourced miss on an incumbent (held office 2022–26) caps that cell below Close. A Record line that does not contradict a 2026 promise stays `📋 Record`, shown, not scored. - **One sentence, one measure.** A sentence already scored on one measure cannot carry a second mark on another, inside or outside its topic. - **Ambiguity resolves upward.** Between two marks, give the higher one. - **Not a source:** frame or tone · a stated lane · bloc membership on other files · third-party endorsement · professional background or a seat held · absence of action (that is Record, not Opposed) · adjacency. **Could this mark be defended to the candidate's face, with the source in hand?** If not, dash. - **Every change goes to** **with a date.** ### Compute reference (Decision 14) **Q1 · shares the goal?** Commits (states an action they will take or have taken) · Agrees (names it as a goal, no action) · Mentions (raises it, no goal → dash, every column) · Disagrees (vote against or explicit opposition). **Q2 · how?** Same instrument · Comparable instrument · A target, no instrument · Neither.
Q1 ↓ · Q2 → Same instrument Comparable instrument Target, no instrument Neither
**Commits** Aligned 3.0 Close 2.0 Partial+ 1.5 Partial 1.0
**Agrees** Close 2.0 Partial+ 1.5 Partial 1.0 Weak 0.5
**Mentions** — — — —
**Disagrees** Opposed −1.0 Opposed −1.0 Opposed −1.0 Opposed −1.0
**Live letter is applied, not computed.** Decision 14 letters (B+, B, C, D, or —) wait for Joa's click. Compute must not overwrite them. The matrix above is how you *propose* a letter to yourself — not how the live card is written. **Propose internally (do not publish as the live letter):** mean of scored answers, at 5 or more. Bands: A 2.75–3.00 · A− 2.50–2.74 · B+ 2.25–2.49 · B 2.00–2.24 · B− 1.75–1.99 · C+ 1.50–1.74 · C 1.25–1.49 · C− 1.00–1.24 · D 0.50–0.99 · F below 0.50. Letters in use on the live card: B+, B, C, D, —. **Cell format, one line:** `Aligned 3.0 · "pattern book of pre-approved duplex, triplex, townhome, and laneway home designs" · https://www.arthurmcinnis.ca/platform · lastmod 17 Jul 2026, retrieved 1 Sep 2026` ## The 12 topics Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date** = lastmod, retrieved. ## Working notes (internal, not for the cell) - **Sources read in full:** [campaign home](https://www.melissacseszko.ca/) (retrieved 2026-09-02) · [About Melissa](https://www.melissacseszko.ca/about-melissa) (retrieved 2026-09-02) · [Updates](https://www.melissacseszko.ca/updates) — one post (retrieved 2026-09-02) · [Victoria News covers the campaign, 15 May 2026](https://www.melissacseszko.ca/victoria-news-campaign-coverage) · [Victoria News launch, 12 May 2026](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/12/business-owner-and-lifelong-victoria-resident-stepping-up-for-city-council/) (retrieved 2026-09-02). - **Read and not scored:** [CHEK, 25 Nov 2025](https://cheknews.ca/fed-up-with-street-disorder-victoria-business-owner-to-run-for-mayor-1291355/) — superseded mayoral-run framing; "I want to make the streets accessible again" / "bring the heart back into the city" restates downtown disorder and downtown economy already allocated, and names no mobility or housing instrument. [CFAX / Adam Stirling Soundbites listing, 12 May 2026](https://www.iheart.com/podcast/1300-adam-stirling-soundbites-304168776/) — 14-minute interview exists; no transcript located this retrieval, so no URL+date quote and no cell. VoteMate Victoria council list retrieved 2026-09-02: no Cseszko profile, no questionnaire. - **Not a source, applied:** five years operating Mel Lingerie on Fort Street, repeated break-ins, Claremont High School, downtown resident, small-business owner (professional / lived-experience background); Our Fernwood and Sustainable Victoria blurbs (third-party); Business Examiner 19 May 2026 one-line notice (third-party); "practical rather than ideological" / "results over ideology" (frame or tone). - **One sentence, one measure — the ledger.** Five sentences carry the five scored cells: (1) "Safety is not just about enforcement. It is about predictability, order, and trust." → row 6 Weak 0.5. (2) "Victoria needs a renewed focus on creating a downtown that is safe, welcoming, vibrant and economically strong." → row 18 Weak 0.5. (3) "It means protecting what makes the city unique: heritage, charm, historic buildings, and local businesses, while making the city function responsibly and efficiently." → row 36 Weak 0.5. (4) "If a program is working, Melissa will support it. If it is not delivering results, she will push for it to be reviewed and adjusted." → row 41 Partial 1.0. (5) "When public money is spent, there should be oversight, transparency, and performance." → row 42 Weak 0.5. - **Contested allocations.** Row 41 Partial 1.0 is the highest mark and the most likely to be argued down to Weak 0.5: she commits to review-and-adjust, which is Commits × Neither, not Agrees. Face-test holds at Partial because the verb is an action she will take. Row 6 stays Weak: "Rebuild Safety" is a pillar title, and the scored sentence names a goal (predictability, order, trust) with no Public Order Team, hours, or command structure — Agrees × Neither. Row 36 keeps local businesses inside the heritage sentence and does not take a second mark; downtown economy is already on row 18. About-page restatements ("public money should be tied to clear results"; "City Hall should be transparent, accountable") are the same accountability cluster as rows 41–42, not a sixth sentence. "Families should feel comfortable downtown" stays context on row 6, not M12. - **Actions found that contradict a 2026 sentence:** none. No City office held 2022–26. Challenger rule applied: 2026 plan taken at face value, no record haircut, no 📋 line. - **Never-list:** no Lisnard / Estrosi / Knafo / Musk / Brivael / Poilievre language used as a source or analogy. - **Rows to put to the candidate before publication:** row 6 (Public Order Team, bylaw hours, or only "standards applied consistently"?) · row 18 (vacancy target, Buy Local, or a downtown mandate?) · row 36 (heritage instrument — design standard, incentive, or listing tool?) · row 41 (does review-and-adjust mean a rotating zero-based cycle?) · row 42 (dashboard, KPI set, publication cadence?) · CFAX (will a transcript or clip with a dated quote be posted?). - **Next mandatory re-check:** after nominations close **11 Sep 2026**, and immediately on any detailed platform release or CFAX transcript. The site carries no lastmod, so re-checks are by retrieval date only. - M83 (civic access / public correction, \$0) has no cell in this 55. Not scored. ## INTERNAL proposed letter — not the live letter **PROPOSE: D** · n = 5 · mean 0.60 Sum of scored marks: 0.5 + 0.5 + 0.5 + 1.0 + 0.5 = **3.0** across **5** scored cells. Mean **0.60**, band **D** (0.50–0.99). D is already one of the five live letters, so no mapping is needed. **This is a proposal, not the live letter.** The card above shows **—**. The live letter waits for Joa's click and compute must not overwrite it. Alignment compute APPLIED for Cseszko stays **—** unless Joa clicks. **What the proposal is measuring.** Not hostility to the Program — she is not Opposed on a single cell — but distance from it. Five cells scored, and four of them are a goal without an instrument. One Partial (programme review) and four Weaks is the arithmetic signature of a platform that agrees in direction and has published almost nothing to deliver with. Fifty cells are dashes because she has not spoken to them, not because she failed them. **Fragility.** At n = 5 the letter is the thinnest that can exist. Drop the Partial and n = 4, so no letter. Read two of the Weaks up to Partial and the mean is 0.80, still D. The mean reaches 1.00 (C− → **C** on the live set) only if the scored set itself changes. Hold the live letter at **—** until after 11 Sep if there is any signal of a fuller platform or a CFAX transcript.
